# 001 — Assets are compiled from recipes, not generated by AI mesh models

Status: accepted
Date: 2026-10-25
Supersedes: —

## Context
The pipeline this project is inspired by started on AI mesh generation (Meshy plus an image model) and froze it. Measured pains:
- Credits per attempt; iteration multiplies cost.
- No reproducibility: same prompt, different mesh. Nothing to diff, nothing to regenerate in CI.
- One fused mesh: no named parts, no pivots, so nothing animates without manual work.
- A texture per asset: a draw call per asset, inconsistent texel density.
- Every mesh needed repair: scale, pivots, holes, topology.
It replaced generation with a recipe compiler, and those problems went away for hard-surface assets.

## Decision
The core path is a deterministic compiler: recipe source → mesh IR → GLB. AI enters as the **author** of the recipe (a coding agent), not as the mesh generator. Mesh-generating models are an optional, cached adapter for what recipes do badly ([idea/08](../idea/08-neural-adapters.md)).

## Alternatives considered
- **AI mesh generation as the core** — why not: the five pains above; outputs aren't reproducible or partitioned into named parts.
- **Procedural modelling in a DCC (Blender geometry nodes, Houdini)** — why not: a heavy external runtime, node graphs agents edit poorly, and no plain-text diff.
- **Kitbashing from asset libraries** — why not: licence per asset, mismatched styles and texel density.

## Consequences
- Easier: free iteration, reproducible builds, named animatable parts, one material, CI gates.
- Harder: organic and sculpted forms (people, animals) are a weak spot. Answered by the planned `creature` kind and `/neural` adapter.
- Revisit when: an open-weight model outputs part-segmented, reproducible, low-poly meshes with consistent UVs on CPU.
